as_told.title: John Burke measures positive surface charge at stone circles

plain: The claim is that ancient pyramids and stone sites in Mexico and Central America, Europe and Egypt give off a measurable energy, and that seeds exposed to it grow much better. A researcher named Jim Weiner tells Michels that researchers found seed yields went up "like three to five times" per acre. He credits a book he calls Seeds of Knowledge, Stones of Power. A researcher named Geoffrey Drumm credits what sounds like the same book under a slightly different title, Seed of Knowledge, Stone of Plenty, by a researcher named John Burke. Drumm says Burke measured the sites with electrostatic voltmeters, instruments that read electric charge, and found a positive charge on the surface, and he puts the measurements at stone circles. He also names another researcher, Hugh Newman. If true, it would mean these ancient sites were built to do something physical, not only to serve as monuments or tombs.
